notes: The map labels its own start and finish, on info_teleport_destination point entities rather than on the trigger volumes, which is why nothing was read out of it automatically. Its shape is a lobby and a course: all 21 info_player_* spawns are in a room at z~13100 beside the `exit` destination, and the only trigger_teleport aimed at `start` is a 975x24 doorway standing in that room -- so the lobby is where you arrive and `start` [5365 -2963 -3770] is where the course begins. The finish is the other end of the same mechanism: exactly one trigger_teleport in the map is aimed at `finish`, it is a 2-unit-thick plane at the far end of the ride, and the destination it throws you to sits back at lobby height next to the `exit` door that returns you. A thin plane a player crosses once, aimed at a destination called finish, is a finish line.

conditional_teleports.note: the map's anti-standing trap: a trigger_multiple on each block sets the player's name to the one this filter passes after a delay and resets it after another, so the teleport only fires on a player who stood on a block too long. This game does not run the map's outputs, so imported unconditionally it fired on every landing. Dropped; standing still is allowed here and costs the player time instead
